Hi Grace / Elena —

Thanks again for the meeting this morning. We need to get a couple of items in place before Procurement can issue the PO from our EU entity (for services performed to support EU customers). To avoid delays, can you confirm the following and return the requested documents?

1) Are you VAT-registered in Kenya? If yes, please attach the VAT registration / KRA PIN and an example VAT invoice that includes the PIN and VAT line.
2) Do you treat the scope of services in our SOW as VATable local services or as exported services zero-rated for VAT? If you believe they are zero-rated, please point us to the supporting reference or guidance you use.
3) Is Kenya requiring an e-invoice or special invoice ID for outbound invoices to a foreign buyer? If so, include an example.
4) For cross-border payments: do you expect any Kenyan withholding tax to be applied by the paying entity? If you have a tax residency certificate (or tax clearance) that would support treaty relief, please attach it.

Attachments we expect from you to complete our vendor file: KRA PIN / VAT cert, sample invoice, company registration, and tax residency/clearance if available. Once we have these, Finance (cc'd) will confirm whether we need to apply withholding or can route the PO without deduction.

If it's easier, you can upload the docs to the Drive folder I'll share or return them in reply. Appreciate a response by COB Wednesday so we can hit the supplier cutover next week.

Cheers,

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are the documents you requested (see attachment stubs below). Quick answers inline:

- VAT registration: Yes, Grace Logistics is registered with KRA. PIN and VAT certificate attached (Grace-KRA-PIN-and-VAT-Cert.pdf).
- VAT treatment: For most cross-border B2B services we treat them as exported services and zero-rated under section 16 of VAT Act (i.e., VAT 0% on invoices to non-resident customers). We will mark the invoice as zero-rated and include the KRA PIN.
- E-invoicing: Kenya's e-invoice rollout is in pilot phases for specific sectors. We are not required to submit a special e-invoice ID for a foreign buyer at this time — a standard tax invoice showing PIN and VAT position is sufficient.
- Withholding: As a Kenyan resident supplier, local WHT can be applied if the paying party is a Kenyan withholding agent. Because Redwood's billing will be routed from your EU legal entity (per our discussion), Kenyan WHT should not be applied. If Redwood's payment originates from a Kenyan entity, different rules apply.

Attachments (embedded as files): Grace-KRA-PIN-and-VAT-Cert.pdf, Grace-Invoice-Sample-USD.pdf, Grace-Business-Registration.pdf

Let me know if you need a Kenyan tax residency certificate — we can request a tax clearance letter from KRA but that takes ~2–3 business days.

Best,

Quick technical note from Tax:

- Kenyan VAT zero-rating for exported services is standard practice when services are supplied to a non-resident and consumed outside Kenya, but the supplier must be able to demonstrate the exported nature of the supply. Grace's confirmation that billing will go to our EU entity and that services support EU customers is useful evidence.
- Withholding: Kenya can impose withholding on certain payments to resident suppliers if the payer is a Kenyan withholding agent. If Redwood's EU entity pays Grace directly, Kenyan WHT shouldn't apply. However, if payment is routed through any Kenyan-based payment processor or agent, we must re-evaluate.
- Recommended evidence pack for our file: KRA PIN, VAT cert, company registration, sample invoice, and a short vendor declaration confirming zero-rated supply to non-resident (signed). If Grace can provide a KRA tax clearance or a recent tax residency letter, that is preferred but not strictly required for PO issuance; it helps Treasury avoid withholding-related holds.

I'll coordinate with AP to set the vendor exemption flags once the documentation is on file.

-Rishi
Head of Tax, Redwood Inference
